subject: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls - FinTrust discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls - FinTrust discovery

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we stay aligned:

- Scope: FinTrust is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing document ingestion and anonymized analytics. Primary concerns: PII handling, data residency for EU customers, and support access controls.
- Must-haves: RBAC with least-privilege, auditable support "break-glass" workflows, configurable data retention policies, and detailed logging for forensic audits.
- Current environment: FinTrust runs in us-west with a subset of EU customers; preference for US-hosted for now but legal team wants residency guarantees for specific EU accounts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to confirm how our break-glass flow works and what audit trails it leaves (see question list below).
2) Send you our SOC2 summary and an access-control diagram.
3) Schedule a 30-min compliance deep-dive with you + your security contact.

Quick questions for the compliance deep-dive so we can prep:
- Do you need full tenant-level data residency for EU, or per-customer region routing?
- Are there specific retention windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days) we should demonstrate?
- Any restricted roles you need us to map (e.g., billing-only, support-read, support-write, admin)?

Attaching a short SOC2 summary and an access-controls diagram for reference (attached).

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi and Dev into the compliance call once we have availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, access-controls-diagram.png

From: Asha Kumar <asha.kumar@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls - FinTrust discovery

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Residency: For our EU enterprise customers we need per-customer residency (data for that customer must remain in EU). For other customers US is fine.
2) Retention: Standard is 365 days for transaction logs, 90 days for raw ingestion payloads, and 30 days for derived analytics (unless legal holds).
3) RBAC: We need granular roles and the ability to define custom roles at the tenant level. Support access must be limited and fully auditable — we need to see who invoked any break-glass and what data was exposed.
4) Support access flow: Do Redwood engineers get any sort of default access? If so, how is that gated (SOW, impersonation tokens, time-limited keys)?

We can do a compliance call next week. Our security lead (Michael Owens) will join. He may also ask for the full SOC2 report and any recent pen-test results.

Regards,
Asha
Head of Product Compliance | FinTrust
asha.kumar@fintrust.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Kumar <asha.kumar@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls - FinTrust discovery

Hi Asha — quick technical answers to your items below. Happy to go deeper on the call.

1) Residency: We support per-customer region pinning for both storage and inference. For EU-pinned customers, data and model artifacts remain in EU regions; routing policies ensure requests for those tenants go to EU capacity.

2) Retention: Retention windows are configurable per-tenant. We offer retention presets (30/90/365) and support legal-hold flags that suspend deletion. All retention actions are logged.

3) RBAC & Custom Roles: Our RBAC supports tenant-scoped roles and custom role definitions. Built-in roles include: owner, admin, billing, support-read, support-write, svc-integration. You can create custom roles and restrict API + Console privileges.

4) Support access / Break-glass:
- Redwood support does not have default access to customer data. Support access is strictly request-based and must be approved by the customer's designated admin unless a pre-agreed SOW grants controlled support access.
- When break-glass is used, access is time-limited (configurable TTL), audited (who, when, reason), and requires multi-party approval for sensitive tenants (e.g., EU-resident).
- All access is logged with request IDs and session replay for forensic review. Logs are retained per the tenant's retention settings and are exportable for audits.

Attached I dropped a short diagram (access-controls-diagram.png) that shows approval flow and audit logs. For SOC2 and pen-test artifacts, Marissa will share the summary; we can provide the full reports under NDA.

Documentation: https://redwood.ai/docs/security/access-controls (includes API examples for creating tenant roles and invoking break-glass)

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
